target: Original Japanese SegaNet Mega Drive build, played through Genesis Plus GX or MiSTer on PC

areas.name: Setup and Core Rules
areas.location_cue: The black playfield with a seven-column grid and a falling four-piece cluster.
areas.note: Use the preserved Mega Drive build through the selected Genesis-compatible emulator route.

levels.1: Use the opening drops to learn movement before the board becomes crowded.
levels.2: Move a falling cluster with Left or Right, accelerate it with Down, and rotate it counterclockwise with B or C.
levels.3: A cluster contains four linked pieces. Shift it before contact, rotate with B or C to change their order around the cluster, and use Down only after its landing column and orientation are safe.

levels.1: Arrange matching pieces so gravity can improve the next match.
levels.2: Place at least two identical pieces edge-to-edge; they vanish and any unsupported pieces above them descend.
levels.3: Make one adjacent pair beneath a different matching pair. When the lower pair disappears, the unsupported upper pieces fall; if they touch their match, the board resolves another clear as a chain.

levels.1: Watch several clusters before assuming the colour set is complete.
levels.2: Confirm the ordinary set: white square, green square, blue circle, yellow upright triangle, red inverted triangle, orange diamond, and purple cross.
levels.3: Record each of the seven shape-and-colour combinations once. Matching uses identity, not approximate colour; the two triangles point in opposite directions and count as different pieces.

areas.location_cue: The Round Mode board whose opening counter shows 00 through 09.
areas.note: Spiral placement is fixed, but the incoming colour clusters vary between attempts.

save_backup.why: This build has no native save, and leaving the session can erase Round Mode progress.
save_backup.detail: Keep one emulator state at the round-number screen and a second at the live opening grid. Replace them only after the next board begins safely.

point_of_no_return.title: The active board closes when it resolves
point_of_no_return.why: A success, timeout, or manual restart replaces the current arrangement.
point_of_no_return.detail: Reconcile the spiral count before the final pair disappears. If the board becomes unwinnable, use A+C rather than spending the remaining timer.

levels.1: Most targets lean right; keep the opposite side open for sorting incoming colours.
levels.2: At the opening of Round 00, count columns left-to-right and heights upward from the floor. The 5 spiral targets begin at: C6 B3, C2 B2, C7 B2, C1 B1, C6 B1.
levels.3: Start by exposing the support line beneath C6 B3; then use C3, C4 as working space while collapses draw the right-side targets together. Incoming clusters vary, so adapt the colour order; use A+C immediately if one spiral becomes isolated. The three-minute clock continues during pause.

areas.name: Solo Endless Modes
areas.location_cue: The mode menu listing Normal, Doubt, and Block beside Round Mode.
areas.note: These score-driven rulesets have no authored final board, so completion records their distinct mechanics and the established Normal benchmark.

levels.1: Build steady chains while leaving one recovery column open.
levels.2: Choose Normal Mode and continue until its level display reaches 10.
levels.3: Normal has no finite board list, so Level 10 is the documented completion benchmark. Clear low and wide, reserve one column for awkward clusters, and reduce fast drops as the automatic speed increases.

levels.1: Expect a landed cluster to change after it settles.
levels.2: Choose Doubt Mode and watch a non-white piece turn into a white square on landing.
levels.3: White squares do not arrive as ordinary falling pieces here. Leave potential white partners accessible, land several clusters until a conversion occurs, then erase the converted square by placing it beside another white square.

levels.1: Build one rigid formation, then look for the match that frees it.
levels.2: Choose Block Mode, land a cluster so it remains supported as one unit, then create a matching pair beneath it.
levels.3: Unlike the ordinary rules, landed clusters can stay rigid instead of separating immediately. Stack a small tower, complete one pair at its support, and confirm that the released formation collapses and resolves any new contacts.

areas.name: Computer Versus
areas.location_cue: The 1P VS COMP menu with a single-digit difficulty selector.
areas.note: The selector exposes ten distinct settings, numbered 0 through 9.

levels.1: Use the slower opening pace to practise clean, low stacks.
levels.2: Choose 1P VS COMP, set the computer difficulty to 0, and finish with the winning field.
levels.3: Difficulty 0 changes the opposing fall pace. Keep your own stack below mid-field, favour two-step chains over speculative towers, and convert any attack window into safe board reduction before pursuing more pressure.

levels.1: A successful computer match opens the game's formal completion display.
levels.2: Win any 1P VS COMP match and remain through the book-style staff pages.
levels.3: After the victory screen, do not reset or load a state. Let the closing transition finish, page through the complete staff display, and wait for its final page before returning to the title.

areas.name: Two-Player Modes
areas.location_cue: The title menu entries labelled 1P AND 2P and 1P VS 2P.
areas.note: Side-by-side play allows different rulesets on the two fields; direct versus uses the competitive rules.

levels.1: Open both playfields and verify the mode can run independently on each side.
levels.2: Choose 1P AND 2P, assign Round Mode, and clear the spiral targets on at least one side.
levels.3: Activate the second controller if two players are present; otherwise leave it idle and use the first field. Each side can choose its own ruleset, so confirm the Round behaviour on the active field before leaving the match.

levels.1: Open both playfields and verify the mode can run independently on each side.
levels.2: Choose 1P AND 2P, assign Normal Mode, and finish with the higher recorded score.
levels.3: Activate the second controller if two players are present; otherwise leave it idle and use the first field. Each side can choose its own ruleset, so confirm the Normal behaviour on the active field before leaving the match.

levels.1: Open both playfields and verify the mode can run independently on each side.
levels.2: Choose 1P AND 2P, assign Doubt Mode, and observe a white conversion on either field.
levels.3: Activate the second controller if two players are present; otherwise leave it idle and use the first field. Each side can choose its own ruleset, so confirm the Doubt behaviour on the active field before leaving the match.

levels.1: Open both playfields and verify the mode can run independently on each side.
levels.2: Choose 1P AND 2P, assign Block Mode, and release one rigid tower on either field.
levels.3: Activate the second controller if two players are present; otherwise leave it idle and use the first field. Each side can choose its own ruleset, so confirm the Block behaviour on the active field before leaving the match.

levels.1: Keep both fields visible and compare safe stack height before attacking.
levels.2: Choose 1P VS 2P and play until the ten-minute clock expires or one field fills.
levels.3: Competitive play cannot be paused. Win by holding the higher score at time expiry or by forcing the opposing field to overflow; keep a clean lane available whenever the middle display signals interference.

levels.1: Build a larger simultaneous clear during a versus match.
levels.2: In a versus match, erase at least five pieces in one resolution to send a concealed cluster.
levels.3: Prepare a connected group of five or more matching pieces, complete the last contact, and watch the opposing preview receive an unidentified cluster whose contents remain hidden until landing.

levels.1: Reserve a very large clear for the competitive field.
levels.2: In a versus match, erase at least seven pieces in one resolution to trigger the stronger attack.
levels.3: Join seven or more identical pieces before completing their contact. The resulting attack briefly interferes with the rival's falling-cluster control, so verify the effect while both fields remain active.
